# Verification analysis: split-dns-authority-alpine

Job: `2026-09-06__00-21-44`

This report explains the verifier decisions recorded for this job. It interprets the saved evidence; it does not rerun the task or independently inspect the expired clusters.

## Task

> Each router answers DNS for the private network it serves. Have `node1`
> resolve the name `app.internal` to `node3`'s address for hosts on `lan-a`,
> and `node2` resolve the same name to `node4`'s address for hosts on `lan-b`,
> so each host reaches the service on its own side of the transit network by
> that one name.

## Environment

- Systems: **1 vyos + 1 opnsense + 2 alpine**
- Networks: **mgmt, transit, lan-a, lan-b**
- Control node: **node3**
- Executor model: **claude-sonnet-5**

## Trial `split-dns-authority-alpine__rSso8Hu`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor successfully implemented split DNS: node1 (VyOS) resolves app.internal to node3 (10.100.13.12) for lan-a, and node2 (OPNsense) resolves app.internal to node4 (10.100.13.13) for lan-b, each verified both locally and from the respective downstream host. All four nodes were also taken through the mandated restart-evidence protocol, with pre-restart baselines, restart acknowledgements, changed boot identities, and confirmed post-restart recovery of DNS and service state, fully corroborated by the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots. Minor hygiene issues include a self-corrected malformed Unbound configuration edit on node2 and some uncleaned backup/log residue files.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.720 | 0.900 | 52/9 (+14 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **node1-resolves-app-to-node3 — Satisfied:** node1 (VyOS, lan-a router) resolves app.internal to node3's address (10.100.13.12) for lan-a hosts
  - **Why:** node1 was configured with a static-host-mapping for app.internal -> 10.100.13.12 plus DNS forwarding, committed and saved (cmd-18c2e895d27a4503). Local dig on node1 and nslookup from node3 both returned 10.100.13.12 before restart (cmd-a22b462711f3414c, cmd-223d4db0dbdc44eb), and the same resolution was re-verified from node3 after node1's restart (cmd-e07ca3fb0ecf4619, cmd-2f043a2d29164296), confirming persistence across a reboot.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-18c2e895d27a4503`, `cmd-a22b462711f3414c`, `cmd-223d4db0dbdc44eb`, `cmd-e07ca3fb0ecf4619`, `cmd-2f043a2d29164296`
- **node2-resolves-app-to-node4 — Satisfied:** node2 (OPNsense, lan-b router) resolves app.internal to node4's address (10.100.13.13) for lan-b hosts
  - **Why:** After correcting an initial malformed Unbound host-override schema (host/domain/ip instead of hostname/domain/rr/server, which broke unbound-checkconf), the executor applied a schema-correct host override, restarted unbound, and confirmed host_entries.conf and live drill/nslookup queries returned 10.100.13.13 both from node2 itself and from node4 (cmd-e5fc7d91506d49a7, cmd-07e60535acb94bf9, cmd-aa0237bdef7b4bc1). Resolution was re-confirmed from node4 after node2's restart (cmd-7a2e89f269ef46b5, cmd-a90b2be18671484b).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-2cb9fa08d25b487d`, `cmd-bd08b3fec8624190`, `cmd-e5fc7d91506d49a7`, `cmd-07e60535acb94bf9`, `cmd-aa0237bdef7b4bc1`, `cmd-7a2e89f269ef46b5`, `cmd-a90b2be18671484b`
- **split-dns-persists-across-restart — Satisfied:** Split DNS behavior (each host resolves app.internal only to its own side's service address) persists after routers restart, consistent with the provider-wide restart-evidence protocol applied to all four nodes
  - **Why:** For all four nodes, pre-restart boot identity and working DNS answers were captured, a restart was acknowledged, polling observed connection loss then recovery, a new boot identity was confirmed, and DNS/service state was re-verified post-restart: node1 (cmd-cf138ea2126c4900, cmd-d57e9b27796b41ad, cmd-dc47e05d7ba5499a, cmd-19ce724438664dcd, cmd-e07ca3fb0ecf4619), node2 (cmd-600c62cba3a244d1, cmd-9462ca46153641b6, cmd-4561e4553ef1491c, cmd-b01b6d9cc4c142a6, cmd-7a2e89f269ef46b5), node3 (cmd-8193576b03a94bd2, cmd-cef262e9a40749d4, cmd-b465be7324f14ef5, cmd-ae3144bb985342ab), node4 (cmd-2ace8a1f8dd14594, cmd-50a3935130344c46, cmd-6bc93fd95fe1485e, cmd-6b1d018bce244e5f). Fixed lifecycle snapshots corroborate boot-identity changes on all four nodes.

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.720**. Most executor mutations were directly tied to the task (VyOS static-host-mapping/dns-forwarding config, OPNsense host-override) or to the mandated restart-evidence protocol, and were fully verified. However, on node2 the executor made an initial malformed Unbound host-override XML edit (cmd-2cb9fa08d25b487d) using an incorrect schema (host/domain/ip instead of hostname/domain/rr/server), which broke unbound-checkconf (cmd-8be984ad59524a74, cmd-04991543366f4ea0) before being corrected (cmd-bd08b3fec8624190); this counts as an unnecessary/incorrect mutation even though it was subsequently fixed and left the service in a working state. The executor also left backup config files (/conf/config.xml.bak, /conf/config.xml.bak2 from cmd-d4b7f0dcc8fe4bc6 and cmd-2cb9fa08d25b487d) and /tmp/reboot.log files on node1/node2/node3/node4 as low-risk residue with no evidence of cleanup. No destructive, broad, or security-weakening mutations were observed, and package/service health checks post-executor show no failed services or package inconsistencies.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-2cb9fa08d25b487d`, `cmd-8be984ad59524a74`, `cmd-04991543366f4ea0`, `cmd-bd08b3fec8624190`, `cmd-d4b7f0dcc8fe4bc6`, `global:after_executor:node1:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node1:package-health`, `global:after_executor:node3:package-health`, `global:after_executor:node4:package-health`

### Comments and limitations

- No direct evidence was captured showing whether backup files (/conf/config.xml.bak, /conf/config.xml.bak2) or /tmp/reboot.log files were cleaned up after use, since the lifecycle temporary-files snapshot only inventories /tmp and does not track /conf.
- Verification queries were run from the routers themselves and from node3/node4 directly targeting the router IPs; no evidence was captured of a client on lan-a/lan-b using the router as its configured default resolver via normal DHCP-provided DNS settings, though this is a reasonable proxy for the same behavior.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.720); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.900; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
